subject: Request: temporary GPU prioritization for Atlas AI demo / Q4 ramp
messages:
From: Sylvia Chen <sylvia@atlas-ai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Short-term capacity need for upcoming demo + Q4 ramp

Hi Marissa,

We’ve got a buyer demo scheduled for Aug 20 and an internal Q4 launch target that would double inference traffic the week starting Sep 6. Can Redwood support a short-term prioritization bump to avoid throttling during the demo window and provide a runway while we finalize our Dedicated commitment?

What we’re asking: a temporary prioritization (or soft reservations) allowing Atlas AI to exceed our current Dedicated pool allocation by ~30% for two weeks (Aug 18–Sep 1), with a clear rollback. We can sign an addendum and are willing to cover overage at list + uplift. I attached a usage summary and a proposed quick pricing sheet.

Thanks,
Sylvia Chen
Head of Cloud Ops, Atlas AI

Karthik — forwarding Atlas’ ask. They want a two-week 30% bump to avoid throttles for an Aug 20 demo and throughput run-up in early Sep. Sylvia included a usage CSV and a proposed pricing sheet.

Quick context: Atlas is currently on a small Dedicated pool (pool-us-e2) with autoscale cap at committed capacity + 10% burst. This request would temporarily bypass that cap for a bounded window. Can we scope options (safety, rollout, billing)? Dev, can you sketch feasibility and rollback plan?

Next steps I want:
- Feasible approach + risk summary
- Estimated cost uplift for Atlas (one-off and per-hour)
- A simple rollback/kill-switch if we see perf regressions

—Marissa
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-12T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Short-term capacity need for upcoming demo + Q4 ramp

On Tue, Aug 12, 2026 at 10:03 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Karthik — forwarding Atlas’ ask. They want a two-week 30% bump ...

Summary of options from runtime side:
1) Temporary priority flag: mark Atlas tenant as high-priority in the scheduler for a time window. This will route their requests ahead of non-priority traffic but still respect overall pool capacity. Low risk; no infra changes.
2) Short-lived pool expansion: allocate spare nodes from non-prod pools into a new ephemeral slice for Atlas (pool-ephemeral-375). Medium risk — possible knock-on for non-prod jobs; needs ops coordination and node warm-up (~2–3 hours).
3) Autoscale policy exception: temporarily lift hard cap to allow up to +40% burst. Higher risk if other tenants spike simultaneously; requires approval from capacity and finance.

Rollback/kill-switch: implement a scheduler toggle and an emergency drain script (drain-atlas.sh) to immediately stop new Atlas allocations and shift requests to a fallback model variant. Both are doable within 30 minutes.

Cost estimate (very rough):
- Option 1 (priority flag): $0 infra ops, marginal token billing uplift; we can bill at +15% overage premium.
- Option 2 (ephemeral nodes): ~$2,200/day for added nodes (US region), prorated.
- Option 3 (lift cap): similar to option 2 but with unpredictable peak costs; suggest commit to a cap of +40% with a hard stop.

I’ve added a small tech note to INFRA-4982 with logs for pool-us-e2 and a script prototype.

—Dev
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-13T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary GPU prioritization for Atlas AI demo / Q4 ramp

Evelyn — please evaluate capacity/finance implications and advise whether we can authorize a controlled +30% prioritization window (Aug 18–Sep 1) for Atlas. I copied their contact so we’re transparent.

Key considerations:
- We need a clear SLA-limited approval and billing uplift.
- Ops must define the kill-switch and runbook; Dev already outlined feasible options.
- Prefer option 1 (priority flag) for lowest risk; option 2 if we need guaranteed throughput.

If approved, we’ll ship a short addendum and a 2-week credits/invoice. Marissa, please hold any commercial commitments until finance confirms uplift.

—Karthik
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-14T15:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary GPU prioritization for Atlas AI demo / Q4 ramp

Thanks — reviewed numbers. Finance and capacity are willing to approve a limited prioritization under these terms:
- Scope: Atlas gets "priority-1" tag Aug 18 00:00 PT through Sep 1 23:59 PT.
- Limit: soft uplift to +35% of current committed capacity; hard stop at +50% (manual intervention).
- Pricing: overage billed at list * 1.25 (pro-rated hourly); one-off setup fee of $1,500 to cover ops work.
- Controls: Dev to implement kill-switch and monitoring alerts; ops on-call notified during the window.

Please confirm acceptance and I’ll queue the billing addendum.

—Evelyn
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Chen <sylvia@atlas-ai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary GPU prioritization for Atlas AI demo / Q4 ramp

Sylvia — we can move forward on the prioritization under Evelyn’s terms. Summary of the agreed plan:
- Start: 2026-08-18 00:00 PT. End: 2026-09-01 23:59 PT.
- Mode: apply priority-1 scheduling tag (Option 1). If Atlas still observes throttling during the first 36 hours, we’ll lift to ephemeral node allocation (Option 2) with Ops approval.
- Billing: overage charged at list * 1.25; one-off ops fee $1,500.
- Safety: kill-switch in place; infra on-call will monitor 24/7 for first 48 hours.

Marissa — please send Atlas the addendum and get signature. Dev — please post the runbook and add the emergency drain script to INFRA-4982. Evelyn — queue billing.

Thanks everyone — I’ll keep this thread for post-mortem notes after Sep 1.

—Karthik
